clue.text: Drink delivered to prison almost enough to get by

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter of the prison word is dropped

parts.note: QUOD is old slang for prison, here missing its last letter
a spirit distilled from sugar cane

explanation.surface: A drink smuggled into jail is just about enough to help an inmate cope.
explanation.walkthrough: The drink comes first in the clue but last in the answer: it is delivered to the shortened prison word.
explanation.definitionFit: A quorum is the minimum number of members a meeting needs before it can legitimately do business.

clue.text: In contact with peacekeepers holding up work

indicators.note: the peacekeepers hold the other piece inside them

parts.note: the United Nations, whose troops keep the peace

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: UN peacekeepers keep in touch while a job is held up.
explanation.definitionFit: Upon, like on, describes one thing resting in contact with another, as in a book upon the table.

clue.text: Super-vile, possibly

indicators.note: possibly suggests one of several arrangements the letters could take

parts.note: the nine letters of the hyphenated word

explanation.surface: Something described as super-vile might be called by another word.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does double duty: the rearranged letters give the answer, and something super-vile is exactly what the answer means.
explanation.definitionFit: Repulsive means disgusting or causing strong aversion, which is a fair gloss on extremely vile.

clue.text: I'm sent back to remove man in field

indicators.note: sent back means turned round, so the letters run the opposite way

parts.note: I'M without its apostrophe
to doff is to take off, as with a hat

explanation.surface: Someone is being sent back to get rid of a man out in a field.
explanation.walkthrough: Mid-off is a cricket fielding position, in front of the batsman on the off side near the bowler.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket the fielder standing at mid-off is himself called mid-off, so the position names a man in the field.

clue.text: Began being snooty about queen

indicators.note: about means going around, so the snooty word wraps the royal letter

parts.note: stuck-up means haughty or snobbish
R for regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: Someone started acting superior when the subject of the queen came up.
explanation.definitionFit: To strike up is to start, as a band strikes up a tune or two people strike up a conversation.

clue.text: Sun going down stops many a trip here

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for Sun, as for Sunday
tumbling is falling down
to block is to stop or obstruct

explanation.surface: As the sun sets, many journeys come to a halt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trip' looks like a journey but is a stumble, which is what people do over these obstacles.
explanation.definitionFit: Stumbling blocks are obstacles, literally things one trips over, so this is where many a trip happens.

clue.text: Danced again, provided with fresh gear

definitions.meaning: first meaning: did a jig once more

explanation.walkthrough: The first sense splits the word as RE plus a past tense of jig, the lively folk dance.
explanation.definitionFit: To rejig is to re-equip or rearrange, while read literally it also means to perform a jig a second time.

clue.text: Clergyman with tin leg

parts.note: a can is a tin container
in cricket the leg side of the field is also called the on side

explanation.surface: A churchman with an artificial metal leg.
explanation.definitionFit: A canon is a cleric attached to a cathedral, a member of its chapter.

clue.text: Simple force put into tuning when time's lacking

indicators.note: put into means placed inside the other word
lacking means going without, so the time letter is removed

parts.note: taken as written
T is the abbreviation for time
to exact is to force or demand payment

explanation.surface: A simple bit of pressure is applied to an instrument's tuning when there is little time.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove T from TUNING to leave UNING, then put the force word inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unexacting makes few demands, so it is easy or simple to do.

clue.text: Ceremonial wedding vow socially acceptable in centre of Paris

parts.note: pomp is ceremonial splendour
I DO is what each partner says at the altar
U means upper-class, hence socially acceptable

explanation.surface: A grand wedding vow that passes muster in the heart of Paris.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Centre of Paris' looks like an instruction to take the middle letters; it is the Centre Pompidou, the Paris arts centre.
explanation.definitionFit: The Centre Pompidou is the modern art complex in Paris named after President Georges Pompidou.

clue.text: Disk jockey touring former province returned under spell

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the whole assembly is read backwards
touring means travelling round, so the jockey letters surround the rest

parts.note: DJ is the usual short form
ex means former
NI is Northern Ireland, often called the Province

explanation.surface: A DJ on tour in an old province comes home bewitched.
explanation.walkthrough: Northern Ireland is commonly called the Province in British usage.
explanation.definitionFit: To be jinxed is to be cursed with bad luck, as if a spell had been cast.

clue.text: Ruin of Italy offering best maxim for the more mature

indicators.note: a ruin is something wrecked, so the following words are broken up and rebuilt

parts.note: all seventeen letters of these three words

explanation.surface: Italy's finest wares have been spoilt, prompting a saying for older people.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb consoles people reaching middle age by claiming the best years start then.

clue.text: Leah's first unorthodox family member

indicators.note: unorthodox means unconventional, so the letters are put in an irregular order

parts.note: all ten letters of the two words

explanation.surface: Leah, the biblical wife of Jacob, was the first unusual relative in some family story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First' tempts a solver to take only Leah's initial letter, but every letter of both words is used.
explanation.definitionFit: A half-sister shares just one parent with a sibling, making her a relative.

clue.text: Vehicle reversing at side

indicators.note: reversing means going backwards, so the little word is turned round

parts.note: taken as written
a side is a team of eleven, XI in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A car backing up at the side of the road.
explanation.definitionFit: A taxi is a vehicle for hire that carries passengers.

clue.text: What happens when I bump car, family's last one

parts.words: What happens when I bump car
parts.note: if I bump the car, I DENT IT

indicators.note: last points to the final letter of the family word only

parts.note: the final letter of family

explanation.surface: A driver wonders what follows when they bump a car, and whose family is last in line.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening question is answered by a short sentence, with IT standing for the car.
explanation.definitionFit: Identity means sameness or oneness, as when two things are said to be one and the same.

clue.text: Come to light part of church after one leaves guide

indicators.note: one leaving means the letter for one goes out of the word that follows

parts.note: to train is to guide, as a plant up a wall
the tall pointed top of a church tower

explanation.surface: A section of a church comes into view once someone departs from the tour guide.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop I (one) from TRAIN, then add the church part after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Transpire, in its original sense, means to become known or to emerge as fact.

clue.text: Devotee of self-restraint dropping in

indicators.note: dropping means letting fall away, so the named little word is removed

parts.note: discipline is self-control
taken as written; these letters are taken out

explanation.surface: A follower of self-control who is no longer taking part.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'of' looks part of the definition, but it links the devotee to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A disciple is a devoted follower of a teacher or cause.

clue.text: Gift of iron band

parts.note: taken as written
Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
a ring is a circular band

explanation.surface: A present of a ring made of iron.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Of' reads as a link word but is part of the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: An offering is something given, especially as a present or religious contribution.

clue.text: Spots walking stick Conservative misplaced

indicators.note: misplaced means put in the wrong position, so a letter of the stick word moves

parts.note: a cane is a walking stick
C for Conservative is the letter that moves

explanation.surface: Someone spots that a Tory politician has lost a walking stick.
explanation.walkthrough: Shift the C in CANE one place along.
explanation.definitionFit: Acne is a skin condition producing pimples, so it is a collective word for spots.

clue.text: Team tucking into food that's baked for little people

indicators.note: tucking into means eating, which places the team inside the food

parts.note: pies are baked dishes
a team of eleven, XI in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A sports team digs into a bake meant for children.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Little people' looks like children; it means fairy folk.
explanation.definitionFit: Pixies are small mischievous creatures of folklore, often called the little people.

clue.text: More than one trial ends with reportedly dodgy sect in custody

indicators.note: something in custody is held inside, so these pieces sit within the other word

parts.note: to die is to come to an end

indicators.note: reportedly means as spoken, so the word wanted only sounds right

parts.note: iffy means dubious or dodgy
a cult is a religious sect

explanation.surface: A series of court trials ends with a suspicious sect locked up.
explanation.walkthrough: The dodgy word is spelt IFFI to match its sound, and it goes with the sect inside the ending word.
explanation.definitionFit: Difficulties are trials in the sense of hardships, and the plural matches more than one.

clue.text: See 11
Stagger times for listeners

indicators.note: for listeners means as heard, so the spelling follows the sound only

parts.note: days are periods or times

explanation.surface: An instruction to arrange shifts at different times for an audience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stagger' reads as spread out over time; here it means stun.
explanation.definitionFit: To daze someone is to stun or bewilder them, which is one sense of stagger.

clue.text: Disturb pedants backing without direction

indicators.note: backing means moving backwards, so the word is read from the end
without means lacking, so the compass letter is removed

parts.note: purists insist on correctness
S for south, a compass direction

explanation.surface: Fussy people retreating aimlessly cause a disturbance.
explanation.walkthrough: Turn the pedants round, then remove one S.
explanation.definitionFit: To stir up is to agitate or cause trouble, which is a way of disturbing things.

clue.text: Finding fault with grave

definitions.meaning: second meaning: serious or dangerous, as of a patient's condition

explanation.walkthrough: 'Grave' sounds like a burial plot next to fault-finding; it is the adjective meaning serious.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both expressing disapproval and being at a dangerous, serious point.

clue.text: Horses bearing angels oddly shed appearance of age

indicators.note: bearing means carrying, so the horses hold the other letters

parts.note: greys are grey horses

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters are thrown away, leaving the even ones

parts.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters of angels

explanation.surface: Horses carrying angels have strangely lost their youthful look.
explanation.definitionFit: Grey hair is a sign of ageing, so greyness is the look of being old.

clue.text: Horse bearing wife is bathed in sweat

indicators.note: bearing means carrying, so the horse holds the wife letter

parts.note: a steed is a horse
W is the abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: A horse carrying the rider's wife is lathered in sweat.
explanation.definitionFit: Stewed, informally, means hot and sweaty, as if cooked in one's own juices.
